sources.note: Nothing. The 'Pronunciation' section (§§2-4, p. 221) gives six vowel qualities with English keywords, says 'As far as my limited observation goes, there are no significant distinctions between long and short vowels. All these vowels, in the vicinity of nasal consonants, are slightly nasalised', one diphthong ai, and three consonant remarks (g, j, h). No mention of stress, accent, tone or pitch anywhere in pp. 221-242; no tone marks or accent diacritics in the transcription (posthumous notes by a colonial Resident, orthography edited by C. M. Doke; the editors' footnote says word-division is u…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page resh1242; Wikipedia 'Reshe language' (wikitext).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology (Wikipedia page is a stub that explicitly lacks phonology). Glottolog lists only Harris 1946 (grammar sketch) and Makinde 2011 as descriptive references, plus Blench n.d., McGill 2009/2012 and Dettweiler & Dettweiler 2002 for classification/endangerment.
